header: Using an OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline with machine learning oﬄine batch inference
content:
batch inference
Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion (OSI) pipelines support machine learning (ML) oﬄine batch
inference processing to eﬃciently enrich large volumes of data at low cost. Use oﬄine batch
inference whenever you have large datasets that can be processed asynchronously. Oﬄine batch
inference works with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker models. This feature is available in all AWS
Regions that support OpenSearch Ingestion with OpenSearch Service 2.17+ domains.
ML oﬄine batch inference
244
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
Note
For real-time inference processing, use Amazon OpenSearch Service ML connectors for
third-party platforms.
Oﬄine batch inference processing leverages a feature of OpenSearch called ML Commons. ML
Commons provides ML algorithms through transport and REST API calls. Those calls choose the
right nodes and resources for each ML request and monitor ML tasks to ensure uptime. In this way,
ML Commons allows you to leverage existing open-source ML algorithms and reduce the eﬀort
required to develop new ML features. For more information about ML Commons, see Machine
learning in the OpenSearch.org documentation.
